verdict.rationale: Isaac documents a simulation-side bring-up path: importing robots from URDF, MJCF, CAD or USD; configuring robot and sensor models and tuning them; built-in controllers, motion generation and kinematics solvers; and a first standalone script to control robots. It also covers adding your own robots, bridging to ROS 2, and hardware-in-the-loop validation. That covers configuration and first motion mostly in simulation, not physical bring-up. Missing for 10: first-party hardware drivers or real-robot bring-up tooling, any evidence supporting the 'hours rather than weeks' speed claim, and independent or hands-on corroboration of a fast bring-up.
